content.text: In Zimbabwe, where financial isolation crippled the economy, COREMERCH rose as a beacon of hope for digital creators. With Stripe, PayPal, and other conventional platforms unavailable, it became clear that a new infrastructure was needed. This guide walks you through deploying a digital store on [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-workers-crypto-payment-webhooks-explained-digital-creators|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]] Pages for free, using the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) or the Edge Commerce Stack ($197), and accepting [[LINK:https://coremerch.[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/github-pages-free-digital-product-store-hosting-explained|GitHub Pages]].io/store/blog/crypto-payment-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-3|crypto]] payments without relying on Stripe or any other restricted platforms. By following these steps, you can build a resilient digital business that thrives in even the most restrictive environments.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The conventional digital commerce stack has failed many creators in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. With platforms like Stripe and PayPal blocked or severely restricted, the need for a sovereign commerce infrastructure became clear. COREMERCH answered this call by designing, documenting, and deploying a digital commerce stack that gives creators full control over their online stores, payment processing, and data ownership. By using Cloudflare Pages, Cloudflare Workers, Supabase, and NOWPayments, creators can build a resilient digital business that thrives even in the face of financial isolation.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store on Cloudflare Pages, you need a few essential tools. First, you'll need a GitHub account to create a repository for your store's code. Next, you'll need a Cloudflare account to create a Pages site and Workers instance. You'll also need to set up a Supabase account to store your orders and a NOWPayments account to process crypto payments. With these tools in place, you're ready to deploy your digital store.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to connect your NOWPayments account to your Cloudflare Pages site. This involves installing a worker that listens for payment events and triggers the delivery of your digital products. You'll also need to configure your Supabase instance to store order data and set up a delivery pipeline using Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive. With this pipeline in place, you're ready to process payments and deliver digital products to your customers.
You can deploy a digital store on Cloudflare Pages in just 4-6 hours using the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97).
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, it's time to go live and process your first transaction. To do this, you'll need to deploy your Cloudflare Pages site and Workers instance, and configure your NOWPayments account to process payments. With your site live, you can start selling digital products and processing payments without relying on Stripe or any other restricted platforms. As you process your first transaction, you'll see the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) in action, with its 48-hour deployment, end-to-end testing, and 30-day support.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your digital business grows, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to keep up with demand. To do this, you can use Cloudflare Workers to add more power to your payment and delivery pipeline, and configure your Supabase instance to handle larger volumes of order data. You can also use Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive to deliver digital products to your customers more efficiently. With these scaling strategies in place, you can ensure that your digital business continues to thrive, even as it grows.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The most important question you'll ask is, 'Can I really deploy a digital store on Cloudflare Pages for free and accept crypto payments without relying on Stripe or any other restricted platforms?' The answer is yes. With the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) or the Edge Commerce Stack ($197), you can build a resilient digital business that thrives in even the most restrictive environments. By following these steps, you can deploy a digital store on Cloudflare Pages and start selling digital products without worrying about platform restrictions or financial isolation.
The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) includes a 48-hour deployment, end-to-end testing, and 30-day support, making it an ideal choice for businesses that need to scale quickly.

If you're looking for more information on deploying a digital store on Cloudflare Pages, be sure to check out the Edge Commerce Stack ($197), which includes a 48-hour deployment, end-to-end testing, and 30-day support. You can also visit the COREMERCH website to learn more about their products and services. For example, you can browse their products at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html and learn more about their Edge Commerce Stack deployment process.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a digital store on Cloudflare Pages, follow these steps: Create a GitHub repository for your store's code and a Cloudflare account to create a Pages site and Workers instance. Set up a Supabase account to store your orders and a NOWPayments account to process crypto payments. Configure your NOWPayments account to process payments and deploy your Cloudflare Pages site and Workers instance. Set up a delivery pipeline using Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive and configure your Supabase instance to handle larger volumes of order data. Deploy your digital store and start selling digital products without relying on Stripe or any other restricted platforms.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the difference between the Sovereign Starter Stack and the Edge Commerce Stack?

The Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) is a basic digital commerce stack that includes a Cloudflare Pages site, a Cloudflare Workers instance, a Supabase account, and a NOWPayments account. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is a more advanced digital commerce stack that includes a 48-hour deployment, end-to-end testing, and 30-day support, in addition to the basic components of the Sovereign Starter Stack.
Can I use GitHub Pages instead of Cloudflare Pages?

Yes, you can use GitHub Pages instead of Cloudflare Pages, but keep in mind that GitHub Pages has more limited features and scalability compared to Cloudflare Pages. Additionally, GitHub Pages may not be as secure as Cloudflare Pages, which includes enterprise-grade security features and a robust Content Delivery Network (CDN).
How do I configure my NOWPayments account to process payments?

To configure your NOWPayments account to process payments, you'll need to install a worker that listens for payment events and triggers the delivery of your digital products. You'll also need to configure your Supabase instance to store order data and set up a delivery pipeline using Cloudflare R2 or Google Drive.
What is the cost of deploying a digital store on Cloudflare Pages?

The cost of deploying a digital store on Cloudflare Pages depends on the specific components and features you choose. The Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is a more advanced digital commerce stack that includes a 48-hour deployment, end-to-end testing, and 30-day support, in addition to the basic components of the Sovereign Starter Stack.
Can I deploy a digital store on Cloudflare Pages in less than 4-6 hours?

Yes, you can deploy a digital store on Cloudflare Pages in less than 4-6 hours using the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97). However, keep in mind that this requires a high degree of technical expertise and familiarity with Cloudflare Pages and Workers.
What is the difference between Cloudflare Pages and GitHub Pages?

Cloudflare Pages and GitHub Pages are both static site generators that allow you to host your website on the cloud. However, Cloudflare Pages includes more advanced features and scalability compared to GitHub Pages, which may be more suitable for small projects or personal websites.
